jobDescription: Our retail bank serves about 2.4 million personal customers. The Group Product Manager for retail payments leads the product managers responsible for debit cards, faster payments and the mobile wallet, owns the payments roadmap and its quarterly business case, works with the risk and compliance teams on scheme rule changes and represents payments at the retail product committee. Three product managers will report to the post holder, so the bank asks for prior experience in a group product manager or head-of-product role with line management of product managers.
requirements: Builds and maintains a payments product roadmap with a quarterly business case.
Works with risk and compliance on card scheme or payment scheme rule changes.
Presents product proposals to a product or investment committee.
Has held a group product manager or head-of-product role with line management of product managers.
Defines and tracks product metrics such as card activation or declined-payment rates.

evidence.text: Product Manager, Cards, Thornbury Building Society (April 2021 to September 2026): owned the debit card backlog and maintained the twelve-month card roadmap, refreshing its business case each quarter with the finance business partner.
Worked with the fraud risk and compliance teams to implement the card scheme's changes to dispute time limits, writing the user stories and acceptance criteria for the disputes journey.
Presented the contactless-limit change and the virtual-card proposal to the society's product committee, which approved both for delivery.
Set up the card activation and declined-payment dashboards with the data team and reviewed them at the fortnightly product review.
Business Analyst, Thornbury Building Society (June 2018 to March 2021): documented requirements for the migration of the mortgage-servicing platform.

Work sample: the 2025 card payments strategy paper, whose cover page names its author as 'Head of Product (acting), Card Payments', with the roadmap summary, the investment request and the committee's approval note.

HR verification note: the job titles Business Analyst and Product Manager, Cards, and their dates at Thornbury Building Society were checked against the employment reference issued by the society's HR department and match the resume.

Reference check summary: the former director of retail products at Thornbury confirmed in writing that the candidate maintained the card roadmap and presented the virtual-card proposal to the product committee.

propositions.text: The candidate maintained the twelve-month debit card roadmap and refreshed its business case each quarter with finance.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the roadmap work and the former director confirmed it in writing.

propositions.text: The candidate presented the contactless-limit change and the virtual-card proposal to the product committee, which approved both.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the presentations and the reference confirms the virtual-card proposal.

propositions.text: The candidate has held a head-of-product role with line management of product managers.
propositions.rationale: The head-of-product wording appears only as an acting title on the cover of a strategy paper the candidate wrote; it gives no dates, appointment or reports, the employer-checked title is Product Manager, Cards, and the qualification rule forbids inferring seniority or role level from a job title.

gold.expectedGap: No employment record shows a group product manager or head-of-product appointment or any line management of product managers; the acting title appears only on a self-authored document.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the employer-checked Product Manager title and the documented roadmap, scheme-change, committee and metrics work; do not describe the candidate as having held a head-of-product role or managed product managers.
followUpTargets: Ask whether the candidate held a formal acting head-of-product assignment, its start and end dates, and how many product managers reported to them.
